verifierProblems.what: The new read-through gate can fail open on the first consent card of a session (this also covers #270, which asks for the same gate). The page judges the words synchronously in show(). In a newly created prompt window, the 'Ember Sans' face (InterVariable.woff2, font-display: block) is still loading at that moment, so the layout uses the fallback face. `seen` is sticky, so if the card fits in the fallback metrics it stays true after Inter loads and the words run past the fold. The window is made lazily and only hidden between cards, so the first card after launch is always shown in a fresh window. Evidence: scratch copy of the built page with a narrower fallback face (Carlito), real windows.ts factory, real controller and real consent.ts cards (relfix-verify/prompt/e2e/e2e-font.cjs). A probe at judge time shows 'Ember Sans:loading'. On 1280x600 and 1280x580 screens the SSH card asked again with changed settings has 478 px of words in a 466 or 446 px body after the font loads, yet Connect is enabled, the hint is hidden and only the fade shows ('<<< YES ON WITH WORDS BELOW, NO HINT'). Real Windows, macOS and RHEL machines without Inter installed fall back to Segoe UI, SF or Cantarell, so any card that loses a line in those metrics passes the gate. With the guard below applied to the same page, the same cards keep Connect off and show 'Scroll down to read it all first.', while cards that fit still enable.
verifierProblems.fix: In app/renderer/prompt/main.ts judge(), let `seen` become true only when the layout is final: `if (document.fonts.status === "loaded" && readThrough(m)) seen = true;`, and re-judge when fonts finish with `document.fonts.addEventListener("loadingdone", judge)` (checked to work on the scratch page). Alternatives: preload the face at page start and await `document.fonts.ready` before the first judge, or reset `seen` on loadingdone. Put the condition in copy.ts (for example `readThrough(m, fontsLoaded)`) and add a unit test that a fitting block with fonts still loading does not count as read.

verifierProblems.what: PROMPT_SIZE.consent (520x600) is the outer window size, because the window is framed and has no useContentSize. The fix agent's evidence that every real card fits (measure.cjs) used `useContentSize: true` on xvfb with no window manager, where outer and content sizes are equal. On Windows the title bar and borders take about 39 px, and on macOS the title bar takes 28 px, so the body gets about 459 or 470 px. The SSH card asked again with changed settings (478 px) and cards with long key paths (454 to 472 px) still scroll there. The gate catches this, but the main remedy the finding asks for (the window shows the whole card) is not met on two of the three OSes. The guide's new line 'It opens big enough to show the whole card' is also wrong there.
verifierProblems.fix: In windows.ts fit, size by content: add the frame (getBounds() minus getContentBounds()) to `size` before fitBounds, either for the consent size only or for both sizes, keeping the work-area cap. Alternatively create the window with `useContentSize: true` and size it with setContentBounds. Then soften the guide's line to 'big enough to show the whole card on most screens'.

verifierProblems.what: connections.ts attempt() sets cancelledByUser for any `!answer.ok` from the prompt window, not only for a user's Cancel or Esc. That includes the controller's own refusals: no window could be made (reveal answers no at once), or a card that fails validPromptCard, such as a server's keyboard-interactive prompt longer than 2000 characters or a host name longer than 255. With runtime.ts now ending kind 'cancelled' silently, these failures make the connecting bubble vanish with no explanation and no Try again. Before the change they at least showed 'Can't connect to build-01 — Connection cancelled' with Try again.
verifierProblems.fix: Tell a user's answer apart from a refusal. One way: prompt-window.ts ask() refusals and the no-window path answer `{ id, ok: false, refused: true }`, and connections.ts sets cancelledByUser only when `!answer.ok && !answer.refused` (a hunk in connections.ts, listed as shared). A refused prompt then keeps the error bubble.
